findings.message: The locked baseline tests were edited to call plugin.pull()/push() directly instead of the registered menu-action Runnables, so they no longer exercise the user-triggered path. acceptance.md says "The baseline's tests are the locked acceptance tests". Yet the diff replaces `leftPlugin.pull!!.run()` / `push!!.run()` (the Runnable registered via addMenuAction) with `leftPlugin.plugin.pull()` / `push()`, and widens `pull`/`push` from `private` to `internal` in Plugin.kt (lines 540, 578) so they can be called. Under the new wiring (`addMenuAction("Pull") { kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() } }`), the original `pull!!.run()` would return as soon as it started the thread, and the assertions would race the worker. The test was moved to match the implementation rather than the behaviour. No recorded reason or approver appears in the packet.

Each Pull/Push menu action or key binding starts an unguarded new thread, so overlapping syncs run concurrently against the same .local and repository files and can overwrite or corrupt state. Each menu action and key binding (lines 44-54) starts a new `kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() }` / `push()` with no lock, flag or single-thread executor. Before the change, `guiContext.uiRun(this::pull)` serialised them on the EDT. Each worker does readLocalRepository → projectToLocalRepository → readRemoteRepository → writeLocalRepository/writeRemoteRepository on the same `${options.repository}` and `.local` files (`File(...).writer()` truncates on open). For example: press ctrl+\ twice, or press ctrl+shift+\ while `dialogConflictResolver` blocks the first worker in `invokeAndWait`. The two threads interleave reads and writes, and one overwrites the other's merged version vectors, or one reads a half-written file and hits the "corrupt. Requires manual fixing" path.

Sync snapshots the project's renames and comments on the worker thread, then later replaces the whole lists, so edits the user makes during the sync are silently lost. `projectToLocalRepository` (called at lines 550 and 589) reads `context!!.args.codeData.renames/comments` on the background thread while the GUI can still change them. The merged state is written to disk (`writeLocalRepository`) and only afterwards applied in `uiRun { localRepositoryToProject(localRepository) ... }` (lines 572-575, 645-648). `localRepositoryToProject` calls `setProjectRenames(newProjectRenames)`, which replaces the whole list. A rename made while the pre-pull script runs, or while the conflict dialog is open, is therefore lost from the project and was never recorded in the `.local` file. Unsynchronised cross-thread access to the JadxCodeData lists is also a data race.

An uncaught exception in the new worker thread ends Pull/Push silently, with no dialog. `kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() }` installs no try/catch and no uncaught-exception handler. Code reached from pull/push can throw: `context!!`, `localRepository!!`, `oldLocalRepositoryItem!!`, `newProjectItem!!`, `ProcessBuilder(command).start()` in `runScript` (throws IOException for a bad script path) and `process.waitFor()`. Before the change, these ran inside guiContext.uiRun on the EDT, where the host application's EDT exception handling applied. Now they go to the default thread handler, which only logs to stderr.

No test covers the new threading: worker execution, EDT marshalling of the conflict dialog, async application of results, or overlapping operations. The mock runs `uiRun` synchronously (`doAnswer { it.getArgument<Runnable>(0).run() }`). The tests call `plugin.pull()`/`push()` directly on the test thread, and each test passes its own conflictResolver lambda, so `dialogConflictResolver`'s `isEventDispatchThread`/`invokeAndWait` branches and the `InterruptedException`/`InvocationTargetException` handling are never run. Nothing exercises the `kotlin.concurrent.thread` wiring at lines 44-54 of Plugin.kt.

New code uses fully-qualified names despite existing imports, and adds a second file-private logger. ConflictResolvers.kt already has `import javax.swing.*` yet writes `javax.swing.SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()` and `javax.swing.SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait`. Plugin.kt writes `javax.swing.SwingUtilities.invokeLater` and `kotlin.concurrent.thread` inline. ConflictResolvers.kt adds a file-private `LOG = KotlinLogging.logger {}` even though `Plugin.LOG` (logger ID `jadx-collaboration`) exists, so conflict-dialog errors log under a different logger name than the rest of the plugin.
